description: What the main window may call. Custom `#[tauri::command]`s need no permission; this is Tauri's own core API surface at its default, plus the two plugins the app registers. `opener:allow-open-url` is granted rather than `opener:default`, which would also carry `allow-reveal-item-in-dir` (a file-manager call knobas never makes) and `allow-default-urls` (which adds `mailto:` and `tel:`). The scope is the second wall behind `openExternal`'s own scheme check: `web_url` is data an adapter mirrored from a remote system, and `file://` or `vscode://` reaching the OS opener would be a remote-code path that starts in somebody's backlog. `tauri-plugin-notification` is granted the same way, one command at a time: `notification:default` bundles sixteen permissions -- channels, scheduling, cancelling, reading back what is on screen -- and knobas makes exactly two calls (the permission question and the permission request), so the two are named here and the other fourteen are doors nothing asked for. Show logs (#747) opens the log folder with `opener:allow-open-path`, scoped to the folder `$APPLOG` itself, not the files in it; the folder comes from the path API, so no command was added. *Open the backup folder* (#1471) opens the profile's `backups` folder with the same grant, scoped to that folder under `$APPDATA` for the real profile and under `$APPDATA/demo` for the demo one (P13), the files in it not included; the folder is `BackupStatus.directory`, already on the wire. The send itself is knobas' own `notify` command (#339), which needs no grant: the plugin's `notify` dropped the handle a click arrives on.
